extracted.intended_audience: IMLS staff, program evaluators, museum administrators, and MFA grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation report appendix describing survey methodology, sample design, and findings about applicant perceptions of the Museums for America (MFA) grant application and review process. Covers representativeness, respondent perceptions, and suggested program improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative difficulty of MFA application process
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents rated whether the MFA application process was similar, more difficult, or less difficult compared to other federal agencies and to state/local and private grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey results: 61% said similar to other federal agencies, 21% more difficult, 18% less difficult. 55% said more difficult than state/local/county grants, and 81% said more difficult than private grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood of applying again
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of whether an applicant is very likely, somewhat likely, or unlikely to apply again to the MFA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall: 82% very likely, 16% somewhat likely. Variations: large museums 87%, medium 82%, small 74%; funded museums 89% vs unfunded 75%; repeat applicants more likely (applied 4+ times 69%) vs first-time applicants (66%). Stability of leadership made no difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of unfunded projects (resubmission/implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether unfunded applications were redesigned/resubmitted, submitted elsewhere (IMLS or non-IMLS), or implemented in whole/part by the museum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Few (14%) reported a resubmitted redesigned application. 3% submitted to other IMLS programs; 36% sought non-IMLS funding (67% of those received funding). 57% implemented the unfunded project or a version of it; higher implementation among art museums (70%) and lower among children/youth museums (38%). Greater applicant experience and prior funding increased likelihood of implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of reviewers' comments for redesign
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which reviewers' comments were useful to museums in redesigning their unfunded projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 65% indicated reviewers' comments were useful for redesigning. Natural history/anthropology (48%) and aquariums/zoos (55%) reported lower usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of full and fair consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents' agreement that their application was given full and fair consideration during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority (81%) believed applications were given full and fair consideration; natural history/anthropology museums were least likely to agree (65%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpfulness of IMLS staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents' perception of whether IMLS staff were helpful in providing feedback and assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 85% reported IMLS staff was helpful; 25% strongly agreed. Museums that never received MFA funding were less likely to agree (80%) compared to those that had received funding (90%). Some respondents wanted clearer guidance on the scope of staff assistance (e.g., draft review, conceptual advice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer score/comment consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about lack of consistency across reviewers' scores and comments (e.g., divergent scores among reviewers for the same application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over half of commenting museums (51% of comments) expressed concerns about review scores/comments; 14% reported mixed messages from inconsistent reviewer ratings (e.g., one of three scores very low and out of sync). Respondents requested clarification on how IMLS handles divergent field reviewer rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise and understanding of projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which reviewers possess appropriate expertise and fully understand applicants' project contexts and museum niches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some respondents reported reviewers lacked expertise or misunderstood unique aspects of projects, potentially biasing scores. Examples include reviewers misunderstanding the role of site visits or disputing budget allocations despite program officer guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived reviewer bias (size or focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception that reviewers may exhibit bias against museums based on size or project focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some respondents felt reviewers were biased against startups or smaller organizations and out of touch with newer organizational approaches; concerns that adverse reviews could jeopardize small organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of decisions / lag time impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about the time between application submission and decision and its consequences for applicant organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long delays in notification can harm smaller/start-up organizations if MFA funding is critical; respondents reported lost time could threaten operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for partial funding option
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestion that IMLS provide partial funding as an alternative to full rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents suggested partial funding would allow applicants to seek local resources to fund the remainder and might better support viable projects that fall short of full funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about reviewers' backgrounds and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestion to provide more information about reviewers (their background and training) to applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents asked for increased transparency about who reviewers are and their qualifications, presumably to build trust and contextualize comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewers or panels but not both (review structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested simplification or redesign of the review structure—either rely on field reviewers or on panel reviewers, but not both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some respondents questioned the gatekeeping role of field reviewers and suggested eliminating field review in favor of panel review where dialogue among panelists can resolve divergent views.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMLS oversight of reviewers (team approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation for increased IMLS oversight or a team approach in managing reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents recommended more active IMLS oversight of reviewers or use of team-based review to reduce inconsistencies and improve feedback quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify application standards and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to make application standards and guidance clearer to applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents requested clearer guidance on evaluation standards to reduce confusion about scoring and to improve applicants' ability to target criteria effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission review or draft feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for a mechanism to review applications before formal submission to identify and fix major problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents asked if applications could be reviewed prior to submission (e.g., draft review), which they believed might help correct obvious issues and improve application quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MFA administrative data as sampling frame
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological standard: administrative application records were used as the sampling frame for the evaluation survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative data included DUNS, institution name, contact info, application year, project type, grant request amount, matching funds, award amount, operating budget, discipline/function; records were examined for consistency and outliers and updated in cooperation with IMLS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposive sampling strategy for survey sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling approach used distinct purposive samples: recent applicants (2007–2010), recent unfunded applicants, and a subgroup of grantees (earliest funded projects 2004–2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: obtain current perceptions about recent applications, opinions on unfunded awards, and project activity/effects data from earlier grantees. Sample selection yielded 1322 MFA applicants with specified subsamples for sections A–F.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB clearance and documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural standard: obtain OMB clearance (Form OMB 83-1 and supporting statements) prior to data collection and address OMB comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RMC provided OMB package including study overview, methodologies, instruments, and statistical method justifications; OMB responded with questions in July 2010 and clearance obtained in September 2010.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online survey administration procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for administering the online survey: email invitations, mailed letters with access instructions, deadlines, follow-up contacts, and technical support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS sent email invitations; RMC mailed 1322 customized letters indicating a three-week deadline. Follow-ups: second email blast, postcards to non-respondents with extended deadline, additional email blasts with access codes. RMC provided technical support and achieved an overall 65% response rate (865/1322).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response rate tracking and section-specific representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Track overall and section-specific response rates and assess representativeness of respondents versus non-respondents across discipline, size, region, application year, and funding history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Section B response rate 66%, Section C response rate 60%. The appendix details over/underrepresentation (e.g., small museums underrepresented, large overrepresented, recent applicants overrepresented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of museum size using discipline-specific operating budget tertiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum size was defined by operating budget quartiles/tertiles within each discipline group to account for budget variability across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating budgets for museums applying 2004–2010 were divided into equal thirds within each discipline to define small, medium, and large; Exhibit A-4 lists cutoffs per discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional grouping standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic regions for analysis were defined using six regions identified by the American Association of Museums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regions and included states are listed (e.g., New England: CT, ME, MA, NH, RI, VT; West: AK, AZ, CA, etc.). IMLS structured outreach around these regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Project duration categories used for analysis: fewer than two years, two years, and more than two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS typically awards MFA grants for one to three years; for analytic purposes the durations were aggregated into the three categories above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project award size categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Award size categories for analysis: small (under $50,000), medium ($50,000–$99,000), large (over $100,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MFA awards range from $5,000 to $150,000; grouping simplifies analysis of project effects and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary activity area classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the primary area where most project resources were spent: programming, exhibitions, collections/digitization, technology/online resources, or organizational activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections and digitization were combined due to overlap and small counts; selection served as a proxy for primary activity area in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of award amount measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking whether the award amount was sufficient to complete the funded project, with response categories no, somewhat, yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess perceptions of funding adequacy for project completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic characteristics to examine
rubrics_metrics.description: List of characteristics used to analyze variation in perceptions and outcomes: museum discipline grouping, museum size, regional location, prior application experience, history of receiving MFA funding, project duration, award size, project type, and perceptions of award sufficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variables were examined for patterns/trends in how museums perceived the application and award process and project effects.
